Possible mitigations:

1. Stop encouraging every event to be one tall instance with a giant queue. Create an automatic overflow instance system and allow event moderators easily ability to rotate between main and overflow instances.

2. Consider creating advice on how best to run events to avoid queuing being a negative experience; such as the importance of hiring more event moderators, enforcing avatar performance standards, keeping worlds performant, etc.

3. Flag priority and general queues better. If an instance works off of a priority queue system, those people in the priority queue should not be listed as being in the general queue.

4. Add an "estimated time remaining" system.

5. Increase the instance cap to 100.

6. Consider adding a "raffle" system, so someone in a queue has a percentage chance of being offered to join. This would make it so that everyone crushing into an instance queue at the start of an instance ends up with an equal chance of getting in, rather than providing those with better hardware or faster fingers with an unfair advantage.

7. Consider allowing groups of a few people to queue together. Whilst this sounds problematic, consider that this would just mean a group joining might inflate the instance's population by two, three, four, so you might end up with a 84/80 instance sometimes, and thus you'd need to drain 5 people to get the next ticketed person/group in.

8. Consider allowing people to show what they're queuing for to their friends.

9. Crashing out of an instance should give you a grace period to rejoin before you lose your slot.

10. Allow people to queue for more than one instance at once.

11. Bring the current (per-community) priority queue payment stuff done on Discords on-app so if an instance is just a pay-to-join thing with a token queue for the clout, at least this is communicated to the people waiting in the fake queue.

12. Discourage queue idling. Being in a queue then failing to join once your number is up needs to have a gentle discouragement mechanic (such as a timeout).

13. Create anti-AFK mechanisms to help event moderators get rid of people who have folded themselves into the corner of a queued instance instead of just quitting the instance. If someone is AFK, it should be possible to see how long they've been AFK for, and it should be possible to specify a kick timer.

details:
Queues are a poorly implemented feature that actively sucks the fun out of attending events in VRChat and drives people off-platform to organize on Discord and third-party priority queues. Queues discourage moving between worlds during an evening, makes trying to attend the same event with others torturous, and places the burden of mitigating the queue on event organizers. The priority queue feature creates an arbitrary social class system of either "who you know" or "how much you want to pay".

Issues:

1. There is no time remaining estimate or other clue what "x/y" means when you join a queue. A queue could be a ten minute wait or a three hour one.

2. There is no reason not to always be in _a_ queue, even for something you're not that interested in attending. This means that someone who actually wants to go to an event has an inflated queue time over someone who is just in a queue because "maybe in an hour my friend group will migrate there". 

3. There is no reason to even be playing VRChat whilst in a queue. Because queuing persists whilst disconnected, you can join a queue in VR, disconnect from the app, reload into the game on desktop and just tab in to check the queue. 

4. Because leaving a world with a queue means potentially never returning, going AFK for half an hour to prevent losing your slot is preferable to actually leaving and freeing that slot.

5. The priority queue system means the queue count is a lie; if a sufficient number of people are being priority-queued in, the queue _will never move_. I have sat in more than one queue of 100+ people for three hours and ended up higher in the queue than when I started.

6. The mitigation for queues is overflow instances, which is a moderation burden (and a minor technical one). It's unclear why, this long into the queue system's life, an automated overflow instance system is not a thing. Readers may recall that an automatic overflow instance was a property of the old "spam join" queue system!

7. There is no assistance for organizing queuing , knowing where your friends are queuing, queuing as a group, etc. Queuing is a solitary experience. In real life, you queue with the people you're attending with! VRChat manages to be _worse_ at this than when some poor group spends three hours outside a Berlin nightclub. This is actually impressive.

8. Queuing massively prioritizes first-come-first-served, so seeing half an otherwise excellent music event disappear due to the threat of otherwise simply not being able to get into the next event creates bizarre situations where second-tier events go from buzzing to dead. You hear people swapping tips on likely heavily-queued instances whilst at perfectly good events. Socially, this just encourages zerg rushing, not a healthy community.

9. VRChat staff at a whim can already arbitrarily set the instance cap far higher than 80. Trans Academy had an event last week that had an instance cap of 100. If queuing is a constant battle and performance is in a far better place than it was half a decade ago, why is the instance cap still 80?

10. Despite this being the internet, not Disneyland, it is for some reason only possible to queue for one instance at a time. This leads to absurd situations where, when attending an event like Shelter, you have to make a call if you want to queue for an overflow or the main instance. Of course with Shelter, the queuing problem is so bad that there's effectively no point to a queue for the main instance, so...

11. Queuing punishes mistakes and system instability massively. If you're in a busy instance and crash, you're done, there is _no_ saving you. This is despite the aggressive buffer of time that anyone who gets a join offer after queuing (about 90 seconds?) gets. Once again, always be queuing. Heck, queue for the instance you're currently in on an alt so you can rejoin if you crash faster.
title: Make the queue feature not just the worst part of IRL clubbing, but somehow even worse
